newsitem.title: UK: Sellers trim prices on UK meal market after data.
newsitem.headline: Sellers trim prices on UK meal market after data.

text.p: Sellers trimmed ex-mill high protein soymeal prices on the UK meals and feeds market following the release of the USDA's 1996/97 end-year stocks report.
The USDA estimated U.S. soybean stocks at 1996/97 end-year at 140 million bushels, unchanged from its February figure.
On Monday Chicago soybean futures hit an 8-1/2 year high and closed limit up on talk that the USDA could cut its estimate by 10 to 15 million bushels.
Brokers said fund buying had pushed the Chicago market far too high and these figures would test just how strong they are.
"We should see the Chicago market limit down, but the funds have some very long positions and it's going to be something of a battle between the fund managers and fundamentals," said one.
High protein soymeal prices ex-mill soared by 10 stg a tonne during the morning, but after the USDA report sellers took four stg out of their prices making the increase eight stg on the day.
Stores would only give prices on request from buyers during the afternoon, but prices earlier had been around eight stg up.
Rapemeal from the Erith mill was three stg up while resellers were three to five stg higher.
Prices at the Liverpool and Hull mills were one stg above Monday's levels.
Corn gluten feed pellets ex-store Liverpool and Portbury were around one stg up while sunflower pellets ex-mill were three stg higher and store around two stg above Monday's levels.
